findings.description: Worktrees made before this PR with a nested name can no longer be removed by this script: the old worktree-create.sh accepted `fix/thing`, which gave `.worktrees/fix/thing` on `feature/fix/thing`. Passing that name is now rejected as invalid. `--merged` only sees the parent `.worktrees/fix/`, which is not a worktree, so it prints a misleading "Kept .worktrees/fix: <main's branch> is not a feature/ branch". The old worktree-clean.sh did clean these; nothing is lost, but you have to run `git worktree remove` by hand.

In `--merged` mode a broken `gh` (not installed, not logged in, no network) is hidden by `2>/dev/null`. Every worktree is then reported as "no PR merged into the trunk shipped its tip" and the script exits 0, so a broken gh looks the same as "nothing merged". It fails safe, but it is inconsistent with the explicit `exit 1` on a failed fetch.

The existing allow rule `Bash(scripts/worktree-remove.sh *)` already matches `scripts/worktree-remove.sh --merged`, so the bulk mode, which deletes origin branches, runs without a prompt. That contradicts the PR's stated intent not to auto-allow it. Not adding an allow rule is not enough: the prompt needs a `permissions.ask` or `deny` entry for `Bash(scripts/worktree-remove.sh --merged*)`.

"the same for every worktree whose PR merged" overstates what `--merged` does: it removes only worktrees whose exact tip a PR merged into GIT_TRUNK shipped, and a worktree with commits after the merge is kept. The same wording is in the scripts/worktree-remove.sh line 4 header. Suggest "the same for every worktree whose tip a merged PR shipped", which matches the table row.

The NAME-validation glob `''|-*|*/*|*..*|*[!A-Za-z0-9._-]*` is copy-pasted into both worktree-create.sh and worktree-remove.sh, with different error wording, so the two copies can drift. This is acceptable given the verbatim-port intent.

`SHIPPED` is computed before the removal and invalidated by hand after it (`[ "$NOW" = "$TIP" ] || { TIP=$NOW; SHIPPED=0; }`). Any new early-exit path added between the two must remember to keep `SHIPPED` and `TIP` in step.

process_issues.description: The PR head moved during the review, from 4b91c9ee516b38e9e1768c1584482c3f49d6bebc (the checkout the reviewers read) to e07c64952db5dfc6c63778da84312847bf7153eb. The new head adds one change: it removes the `Bash(scripts/worktree-clean.sh*)` allow rule from .claude/settings.json. No reviewer saw that change; the orchestrator checked it against `gh pr diff`. Every finding was re-checked against the new diff, the scripts are unchanged, and the settings.json nit was re-anchored to line 20.
